name: Ivorian French
notes: Ivorian French (Abidjan) as a thin variant of Metropolitan French (fr-FR). One feature is stated, from the PFC survey of Abidjan (PFC page, d) 1)): patte = pâte, so ⟨â⟩ is [a] here and [ɑ] in fr-FR. The same page records brin ≠ brun with a very marked timbre difference at Abidjan, and fr-FR already keeps /ɛ̃/ and /œ̃/ apart. NOT MODELLED: everything else about Ivorian French (vowel quality, the mid vowels of épée ~ épais, which the page says vary a great deal at Abidjan, consonants, rhythm). The page is a survey summary at one point and not a description of every Ivorian variety.

sources.author: Projet PFC (Phonologie du français contemporain), FLORAL-PFC
sources.title: Le français expliqué: Prononciation, I. Le système vocalique, d) Variation
sources.notes: READ (open web page; the page metadata gives 2010 as its publication year and 2017 as its last change). The page reports, from PFC survey points: patte ≠ pâte by LENGTH at Neuchâtel (Switzerland) and Tournai (Belgium) and by timbre at Nyon; patte = pâte at Brunoy and Abidjan; brin ≠ brun kept at Tournai and Nyon (very slight timbre difference), at Toulouse and Abidjan (marked), and fading among young speakers at Neuchâtel; the length opposition faites [fɛt] ~ fête [fɛːt], belle ~ bêle, nu ~ nue, vit ~ vie at Neuchâtel. The page cites Gadet (1996) and Léon (2007).

ancestors.notes: Standard Metropolitan French, the base of every other variety here.
